value: endogenous leaf GA3 content (HPLC) varied with light quality: highest under far-red and blue light, lowest under red light and the 1:1 red:far-red mix (Figure 5A); the Results add that ABA peaked under red light while blue and far-red significantly reduced ABA, and that seedling height was significantly promoted only under blue and 1:2 red:far-red (p < 0.05), with red, far-red and 1:1 showing no significant height effect against white light; the Results give no significance value for the GA3 differences in text (Figure 5 marks differences from white light with asterisks)
method: three months of LED light-quality treatments (white WL, blue BL, red RL, far-red FrL, red:far-red 1:1 and 1:2) at one printed photon flux; leaf GA3 and ABA extracted, C18 solid-phase purification, quantified by HPLC (RIGOL L3000); one-way ANOVA with LSD post-hoc tests, alpha 0.05
conditions: one-year-old clonal seedlings, 12 h photoperiod (06:00 to 18:00), photon flux printed as 400 'mmol' m-2 s-1 (presumably umol), hormones on three randomly chosen seedlings per treatment (each one biological replicate); the abstract says red light and 1:1L increased root collar diameter, but Results 3.1 reports no root-collar-diameter result for 1:1L (the Results sentence on root collar diameter, 134 characters, concerns red light as greatest and is not quoted); the abstract's claim is therefore not carried as a result of this record

value: stem robustness (stem mass per length) rose with higher photon flux density (PFD) and fell slightly at low red:far-red ratio (R:FR) in the text, but Table 6 gives R:FR no significant effect on stem mass per length (0.039, unmarked) and PFD a significant one (0.126, **); across Table 6 the R:FR term is significant for 11 of 24 characters (growth mass/day 0.202***, leaf area/stem length 0.242***, leaf width/length 0.157**, leaf area 0.138**, % leaf allocation 0.092**, palisade cell length 0.089*, stomatal conductance 0.079* where PFD is not significant, % stem allocation 0.070*, stomatal density 0.062*, internode length 0.057*, growth mass/mol 0.056*), and the low R:FR treatments depressed growth rate (mass/day) at both PFD while PFD itself was not significant for mass/day (0.023); the abstract nevertheless says spectral quality did not influence growth and development very much, and the text puts R:FR's contribution at about half that of PFD
method: shadehouse light treatments crossing PFD and R:FR (six treatments including full sun), seedlings harvested after about 429 to 441 days; two-way ANOVA coefficients of determination in Table 6

value: early-instar (second-instar) gypsy moth Lymantria dispar induced more nitrogen-containing volatiles and most terpenoids than late-instar caterpillars; the four compounds that differed between fifth-instar L. dispar and L. populi ((E)-beta-caryophyllene, 3-methylbutyraldoxime, myrcene, nerolidol) were all emitted in greater amounts after L. dispar damage; the mixed-species treatment did not differ significantly from L. populi alone (null), while (E)-beta-caryophyllene, 3-methylbutyraldoxime, (Z)-3-hexenol and nerolidol were emitted less by the mix than by L. dispar alone; feeding intensity significantly affected most monoterpenes, nerolidol, (E)-beta-caryophyllene, most nitrogen-containing compounds and (Z)-3-hexenyl acetate but not DMNT, benzyl alcohol or benzene ethanol; in the temporal experiment green leaf volatiles such as (Z)-3-hexenyl acetate declined after the caterpillars were removed at 48 h, while terpenoids kept being emitted for hours after removal, in some cases to the end of the 96 h record
method: temporal experiment: 15 fourth-instar L. dispar per tree for 48 h, volatiles collected in 6 h intervals over 96 h; species and stage experiment: control, second-instar L. dispar (about 60 larvae, 3000 mg), fifth-instar L. dispar, fifth-instar L. populi and a mix, 48 h feeding then a 4 h collection at 48 to 52 h
conditions: 10 trees per treatment (herbivory and control) in the temporal experiment, 5 trees per treatment in the five-treatment experiment; young trees grown from stem cuttings of old-growth trees, no clone or cultivar named; the quote is the Discussion's statement of the instar result, the Results sentence (about 250 characters) is not quoted; feeding intensity was a PCA measure of leaves damaged and lesion number; no diel record is filed from this paper
